Preface

前言

Preface前言

IN THEORY, CREATING A NEW PRODUCT or introducing a new process is simple. In reality, those of us who actually do it for a living know that it is becoming increasingly chaotic.

从理论上讲，创造一款新产品或引入一套新流程很简单。可实际上，靠这行吃饭的人都知道，这件事正变得越来越混乱。

97 Things Every Project Manager Should Know is a collection of wisdom from project managers, software developers, and a wide range of other occupation holders from all around the world who are successful in managing their teams to success. They have shared what they think are important tips for you to know, whether you are involved in trying to create the product or manage the processes of your organization's projects.

《项目经理应知的 97 件事》汇集了来自世界各地的智慧，贡献者包括项目经理、软件开发人员，以及各种其他职业的从业者——他们都成功地带领团队取得了成功。无论你是在参与创造产品，还是在管理组织项目的流程，他们都把自己认为你应当知道的重要心得分享了出来。

Traditional books teach theory. In this one, people who are actively working in the field day to day share the best secrets that they have learned or developed after years on the job. You can find practical suggestions to improve both the final product and your personal experiences by taming the chaos and guiding the project to a successful completion.

传统书籍讲授理论。而这本书里，是那些日复一日奋战在一线的人，分享他们在多年工作中摸索、总结出的最佳秘诀。你会找到切实可行的建议，既改善最终产品，也改善你自己的体验——驯服混乱，把项目引导向成功收尾。

As I talk to active practitioners, I find that there is a growing trend to involve software developers, research chemists, construction foremen, and all manner of other industry-specific technical experts in projects in a more vocal and active way. Users, and other stakeholders, must also be included in this ever-more-democratic vocation. While this cooperation is great, it multiplies the complexity of trying to get the work finished.

当我和一线从业者交流时，我发现一个越来越明显的趋势：软件开发人员、研究化学家、建筑工地工头，以及各行各业的技术专家，都正以更有发言权、更积极的方式参与到项目中。用户和其他利益相关者也必须被纳入这个日益民主化的职业之中。这种协作固然很好，但它也让「把活干完」这件事的复杂度成倍上升。

— p.25 —

Interestingly, when editing this book I have found that regardless of industry, project role, or worldwide location, those of us who have project responsibilities face the same challenges. And the joy has been that these tip authors from around the world have been willing to share their ideas to help us master those challenges. Since they represent not only project managers, but the voices of those new technical stakeholders in the project, this is your chance to hear their ideas and concerns before facing similar participants in your workplace.

有趣的是，在编辑这本书时我发现：无论身处哪个行业、担任什么项目角色、位于世界哪个角落，背负项目责任的我们面对的都是同样的挑战。令人欣喜的是，这些来自世界各地的心得作者愿意分享他们的想法，帮助我们掌握应对之道。由于他们不仅代表项目经理，也代表项目中那些新兴技术相关方的声音，因此在你工作场所遇到类似的人之前，这是你先一步聆听他们想法与关切的机会。

Based on my firm belief that shared knowledge is power, this book was created by combining the work of authors from 29 United States locations and 12 other countries around the world. The authors have donated their thoughts and advice to help others in the field grow and prosper through more skillful project guidance.

基于我「共享知识就是力量」的坚定信念，这本书汇集了来自美国 29 个地区和世界其他 12 个国家作者的作品。作者们无偿献出了自己的思考与建议，帮助本领域的同行通过更娴熟的项目引导而成长、兴盛。

It is a testament to the intensity of today's belief in the value of a collaborative environment that, despite wrestling with their own daily issues, these authors were still willing to take the time to help us all benefit from their wise, field-tested solutions.

这些作者自己也在应付日常的种种难题，却仍然愿意抽出时间，让我们都能从他们经过实战检验的睿智方案中受益——这本身就证明了当今人们对协作环境价值的强烈认同。

— p.26 —

Licensing note: Each tip is licensed under Creative Commons, Attribution 3, meaning you may reuse the individual contributions in your own work as long as you credit the original author. Each contribution is self-contained and works both in this collection and on its own.

授权说明：每篇心得均采用知识共享署名许可（CC BY 3.0）发布，只要你注明原作者，便可在自己的作品中复用单篇内容。每一篇都自成一体，既能收入这本合集，也能独立成立。

Acknowledgments致谢

The idea for 97 Things Every Project Manager Should Know was not conceived in a vacuum. The series editor, Richard Monson-Haefel, suggested I write this book as a companion to his own book, 97 Things Every Software Architect Should Know. A public wiki was created on the O'Reilly Media website so that anyone around the world who wished to participate could contribute. I am deeply grateful to those who donated their time and tips.

本书的想法并非凭空产生。系列编辑 Richard Monson-Haefel 建议我写这本书，作为他自己《软件架构师应知的 97 件事》的姊妹篇。O'Reilly Media 在其网站上建立了公开 wiki，让世界各地愿意参与的人都能投稿。我深深感谢所有献出时间和心得的人。

O'Reilly deserves credit for listening to this idea with open ears, backing this largely untested way of creating a book, and agreeing that all content would be open source.

O'Reilly 值得称道：他们欣然倾听这个想法，支持这种几乎未经检验的写书方式，并同意所有内容都以开源方式发布。

— p.27 —
